subject: Urgent: Starter Rate Reprieve for NovaBiome Clinical Pilot
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: Starter Rate Reprieve for NovaBiome Clinical Pilot

Team — quick summary and ask:

NovaBiome (Tara Hsu) is asking for an aggressive starter credit and a packaging tweak for a 6-week clinical imaging pilot that kicks off next month. Key points from the call this morning:
- Pilot scope: 6 weeks, ~200k tokens/day peak inference (batch + streaming), expects bursty spikes tied to clinical imaging sessions.
- Request: 60% starter credit on token price for pilot period + ability to be billed as compute-only (no per-seat fees) during pilot.
- Rationale (customer): tight budget window for the pilot; they believe high early telemetry will surface a multi-region, multi-month rollout. They positioned this as an opportunity to be a reference in cardiology imaging.

I pushed back on 60% as a standard ask and asked for a short internal memo (business case + econ). They asked for an answer by EOD tomorrow to keep the pilot schedule.

Attachments: NovaBiome_Pilot_SOW.pdf (SOW, redacted PHI note), novabiome_forecast_v1.xlsx (customer forecast).

Ask: Need an approval path recommendation. My initial thinking is: approve a constrained starter credit with a clear cap + make-good clause (clawback if they convert to lower-commitment later). Marissa, can you prepare an exec memo for CFO signoff? Karthik, can you provide econ sensitivity (30% vs 40% vs 60%) and a suggested cap? Jordan — are there any known legal / procurement flags with compute-only pilot billing?

Thanks — I know this is tight. I flagged it because the customer is strategic in imaging and the reference potential is real.

— Olga
Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: Urgent: Starter Rate Reprieve for NovaBiome Clinical Pilot

Thanks for the heads-up, Olga.

High-level thoughts:
- We should avoid a blanket 60% unless there's a concrete conversion path. That level is typically reserved for large strategic partnerships with multi-year commitments.
- For a 6-week pilot I’d consider a tiered approach: 40% starter credit up to a $40k cap, then reduced credit after that. Alternatively, 50% with a clear 3-month commitment if they convert within 90 days.
- Need clarity on expected ARR conversion rate from pilot and whether marketing/clinical reference activities are part of the deal (i.e., do we get joint PR or case study rights?).

Karthik — can you run a quick unit-econ table (showing incremental gross margin impact at 30/40/50/60% starter credit) so we have something to present to finance?

Jordan — loop in Legal if compute-only billing changes our standard contract template (procurement and auditability).

I'll draft a 1-pager memo for the CFO if we land on a recommendation. If the ask ends up >45% we’ll need VP/CFO signoff.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Adding the econ sensitivity that Marissa requested — quick back-of-envelope: (numbers illustrative)
- Baseline token price (hosted): $0.00008 / token
- Pilot expected consumption: 200k tokens/day * 42 days = 8.4M tokens (~$672 baseline) — note baseline seems low because of short tokens; assume effective billed units ~8.4M and additional inference overhead applies.

Starter credit scenarios (impact to gross margin, simple):
- 30% credit: revenue loss ~ $200, gross margin delta acceptable, minimal runway risk, preserves conversion levers.
- 40% credit: revenue loss ~ $270, moderate pressure on short-term unit economics; acceptable with a capped $40k limit and 30-day invoice terms.
- 50% credit: revenue loss ~ $336; would require a firm conversion trigger (3-month commit or purchase order) or a clawback clause.
- 60% credit: revenue loss ~ $403; only acceptable with firm 6-12 month commit or explicit marketing/reference deliverable and exec approval.

Recommendation: Approve up to 35% starter credit with a $50k program cap and include a 90-day conversion window. Add a clawback if they fail to convert and require joint reference activities to be signed in writing. If Marissa wants the 40%+ path, escalate for VP/CFO signoff.

I can produce a one-page econ sheet for the exec memo (will attach). Also tagging finance to confirm the math (I used conservative inference overhead).

— Karthik

Thanks — good input. Per Karthik’s sensitivity, here’s the ask I want in the memo for CFO:

Recommendation for CFO signoff (draft):
- Approve a 35% starter credit for the 6-week pilot, capped at $50,000 total credit.
- Billing: compute-only pilot billing (no seat charges) for pilot duration; standard contract terms otherwise.
- Conversion triggers: if customer provides a signed purchase order for a 6-month commitment within 90 days, apply a retroactive reconciliation (clawback forgiveness).
- Marketing reference: obtain written agreement for a joint case study and a short testimonial from the clinical lead if they convert.
- Legal: include an audit clause for pilot telemetry and a confidentiality addendum in SOW.

Marissa — can you finalize the one-page memo with econ summary and present to CFO. Karthik — please attach your econ sheet. Jordan — please confirm no procurement blocker for compute-only billing.

If CFO approves, I’ll send a short customer note with the caveats. If they decline, ask will be: either standard rates or 30% with an additional credit if they sign an extended commitment.

— Olga
